subject: Ops metric runbook for Dedicated throughput + pricing ask
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@retailco.com>
To: chloe.martin@redwood.com
Cc: Procurement <procurement@retailco.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Dedicated commit - throughput/latency guarantees and acceptance testing

Hi Chloe,

We're evaluating Redwood Dedicated for a multi-region search+recommendation workload and need clarity before we proceed with a reserved commit. Specifically:

- Can you commit to a tokens/sec and requests/sec target for a 4-GPU pool running the gpt-3.5-like model variant? We expect mixed short (16 tokens) and medium (128 tokens) seq lengths.
- What's your measured p50/p95/p99 latency for 1-3 concurrent requests and for bursty 50rps traffic?
- How do you define the acceptance window for throughput verification (sample size, test harness, time windows)?
- What discounts are available for a 12-month reserved commit (starting bands: 200M tokens/mo, 1B tokens/mo)?

We'd like concrete acceptance criteria we can sign off on with procurement. I've attached a short acceptance checklist (we can adapt).

Thanks,
Samir
Senior SRE, RetailCo

Attachment: acceptance_checklist.csv (see attached)
From: chloe.martin@redwood.com
To: Samir Patel <samir@retailco.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 11 Jun 2028 11:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit - throughput/latency guarantees and acceptance testing

Hi Samir — thanks for the clear list. I looped in Ben (commercial lead) and Karthik (performance/R&D) to put forward a measurement-first proposal. High level:

- We propose a tokens/sec floor and an operational throughput validation run (details below).
- We'll offer tiered commit discounts tied to validated baseline throughput and sustained rate during the acceptance window.
- Acceptance testing will be run in your target region against a customer-supplied traffic profile (we can use your sample traces) and our reference harness.

Ben & Karthik — can you draft the runbook (sample size, windows, pass/fail criteria, artifacts) and a commercial table (commit bands -> discount) we can send to Samir?

Chloe
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: ben.carter@redwood.com
To: chloe.martin@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 09:30:00 -04:00
Subject: FW: Dedicated commit - throughput/latency guarantees and acceptance testing (runbook & discount stub)

Chloe / Karthik — draft below. This is intentionally conservative to avoid SLA churn; we can move numbers after one test pass. Please review and flag any tech objections.

Proposed commercial bands (12-month reserved):
- Band A: 200M tokens/mo -> 18% discount vs retail hosted rates
- Band B: 500M tokens/mo -> 26% discount
- Band C: 1B tokens/mo -> 34% discount + 30-day ramp credit structure

Throughput guarantees (per 4-GPU pool running v1 quantized gpt-3.5-like):
- Steady-state floor: 9,000 tokens/sec aggregate (mixed seq distribution, see test plan)
- Burstable RPS: maintain 40 rps sustained for 60s windows with p95 latency <= 220ms
- Latency targets (per request, single-model path): p50 <= 85ms, p95 <= 220ms, p99 <= 400ms (measured on the acceptance harness)

Acceptance / measurement methodology (summary):
1) Test harness & data: Redwood runs our harness in your VPC (or our dedicated environment if preferred) using your trace weights or our sample profile (attached).
2) Sampling window: 1-hour official run composed of five 12-minute sub-windows; each sub-window must hit the steady-state tokens/sec floor and not exceed 5% error on the aggregate metric.
3) Statistical confidence: require at least 30k requests sampled across the hour; if your traffic pattern is too bursty we extend to 3 hours with the same sub-window structure.
4) Reproducibility artifacts: full trace logs, KV cache hit ratios, GPU utilization, and token-service breakdown by latency bucket (we'll provide CSVs).
5) Dispute resolution: a second run with Redwood engineers and a customer witness; if disagreement remains, neutral third-party run (cost split).

Attachments to include in customer email: retailco_throughput_test_plan.csv (test profiles + seq distribution), retailco_commit_term_sheet_v1.pdf (commercial table + SLO language).

Karthik — confirm the acceptance window math and the tokens/sec floor. If you think floor should be 10k tokens/sec we can discuss tightening.

Ben
Head of Commercials, Redwood Inference
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, chloe.martin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 12:10:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: FW: Dedicated commit - throughput/latency guarantees and acceptance testing (runbook & discount stub)

Ben / Chloe — reviewed. A few technical clarifications and minor edits:

- Tokens/sec floor: we can commit to 9,500 tokens/sec (4-GPU aggregate) for the mixed profile if we run the acceptance harness with the same driver and kernel binaries we ship in production. Caveat: quantized model variant may vary by ~5% on short sequences; we'll surface the variant used in the artifacts.
- Sampling: prefer 3 x 20-minute windows (closer to production duty cycles) instead of 5x12 to reduce variance from startup noise. Keep the 30k request minimum.
- Latency: p95 target of 200ms is achievable in our staging with the sample profile; I'll set acceptance at p95 <= 220ms (as Ben suggested) for contractual headroom.
- Measurement tooling: we'll provide a reproducible script (k8s job + load driver) and a signed hash of the binaries used. Customer can replay the driver locally for verification.

I'll update the CSV with the exact profile and note the binary hash. If RetailCo wants a stricter tokens/sec floor (10k+) we should ask for a one-off performance uplift fee to recompile kernels for their cluster.

Karthik
Sr. Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: chloe.martin@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Dedicated commit - throughput/latency guarantees and acceptance testing

Hi Samir — consolidated proposal below and attached the test plan + term sheet. Thank you for the patience while we coordinated internally.

Commercial proposal (12-month reserved, 4-GPU pool):
- Band A: 200M tokens/mo -> 18% discount
- Band B: 500M tokens/mo -> 26% discount
- Band C: 1B tokens/mo -> 34% discount + 30-day ramp credit structure

Operational guarantees (acceptance pass required to lock the band):
- Tokens/sec floor (mixed profile): 9,500 tokens/sec aggregate
- Burstable sustained RPS: 40 rps for 60s windows (p95 <= 220ms)
- Latency targets during acceptance: p50 <= 85ms, p95 <= 220ms, p99 <= 400ms

Acceptance / measurement methodology (high level):
- We'll run the Redwood harness in your region using the attached profile. Official acceptance is three 20-minute windows (consecutive), with at least 30k requests sampled. Each 20-minute window must meet the tokens/sec floor and latency targets. Artifacts (logs, GPU utilization, binary hashes) will be provided.
- If the native profile is highly bursty, we will extend to a 3-hour protocol to ensure statistical validity.
- Disputes escalate to a joint replay; if unresolved, a neutral run may be executed (costs split).

Next steps: please review attached retailco_throughput_test_plan.csv and retailco_commit_term_sheet_v1.pdf. If acceptable, we'll provision a test slot and schedule the acceptance run next week.

If you want a tightened floor (10k tokens/sec) we can provide a separate uplift BOM and timeline; commercial details in the term sheet.

Thanks,
Chloe Martin
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0193
